questions.question: What is a direct democracy?
choices: Rule by a hereditary sovereign
Government by military officers
A system in which citizens vote on policies themselves
A system in which appointed judges choose all laws

questions.question: What is representative democracy?
choices: A system in which voters choose officials to make public decisions
A system in which one ruler holds unrestricted authority
A system in which only religious leaders may govern
A system in which public offices pass through inheritance

questions.question: Which term describes government by a small group?
choices: Democracy
Monarchy
Anarchy
Oligarchy

questions.question: What distinguishes an absolute monarchy from a constitutional monarchy?
choices: An absolute monarch is selected through competitive legislative elections
An absolute monarch rules without meaningful constitutional limits
An absolute monarch serves mainly as a ceremonial head of state
An absolute monarch must retain the elected parliament's confidence

questions.question: Which term describes a government claiming authority through religious law or religious leadership?
choices: Theocracy
Federation
Republic
Confederation

questions.question: What is a unitary system?
choices: A system requiring two equal national legislatures
An alliance of fully independent governments only
A system concentrating constitutional governing authority in the national government
A system dividing sovereignty equally among all cities

questions.question: What characterizes a confederation?
choices: A monarch appoints every regional leader
All local governments are abolished
A single city governs all national affairs
Member states retain substantial authority while delegating limited common powers

questions.question: Why can a constitutional monarchy also be a democracy?
choices: Monarchs must personally approve every vote
Elected institutions may govern while the monarch has limited powers
A hereditary title automatically guarantees free elections
Democracy requires the absence of every ceremonial office

questions.question: What commonly distinguishes a parliamentary system from a presidential system?
choices: The executive usually depends on support within the legislature
The legislature is prohibited from making laws
Courts appoint all members of parliament
The executive must inherit office from a parent

questions.question: What is a defining feature of federal government?
choices: All regional authority can be withdrawn by any mayor
National laws are written by foreign governments
Constitutional authority is divided between national and regional governments
Local officials hold every national office simultaneously

questions.question: Why is holding an election alone not enough to establish democratic government?
choices: Elections are possible only in monarchies
Democracies cannot have political parties
Public participation is unrelated to democratic institutions
Competition, rights, and fair procedures also matter

questions.question: How does an authoritarian government commonly limit public influence?
choices: By guaranteeing equal access to independent media
By restricting meaningful opposition and concentrating political power
By requiring all policies to receive a direct public vote
By giving courts complete independence from political pressure

questions.question: What distinguishes a republic from a hereditary monarchy in basic classification?
choices: The head of state does not hold office by hereditary royal right
A republic must have exactly two political parties
A republic cannot use elected representatives
A republic must divide territory into independent countries

questions.question: Why might a very large country rely mainly on representative rather than direct democracy?
choices: Representation removes the need for citizens' rights
Direct voting is legally impossible on any issue
Representatives can handle many complex decisions for a large population
Elected officials cannot be held accountable by voters

questions.question: How does totalitarian rule differ from a government that merely limits political competition?
choices: It requires an independent press to oversee rulers
It leaves ideology and private life outside state interest
It prevents the state from organizing public institutions
It seeks extensive control over public and private life

questions.question: A country has an elected parliament and a monarch with ceremonial duties. Which description fits best?
choices: Absolute monarchy
Democratic constitutional monarchy
Military dictatorship
Theocratic confederation

questions.question: A national constitution protects regional governments' powers from ordinary national repeal. Which structure does this suggest?
choices: Federal system
Unitary system
Direct democracy
Absolute monarchy

questions.question: A prime minister loses a vote of confidence and must resign or seek a new election. Which arrangement does this illustrate?
choices: An absolute monarchy's succession rule
A presidential lifetime appointment
A parliamentary executive's dependence on legislative support
A court's power to choose all national legislators

questions.question: Why can the labels democratic and federal describe the same country?
choices: Both describe the length of an executive's term
Both refer to the method used to select judges
Both describe the number of parties represented in a legislature
One concerns participation; the other concerns territorial authority

questions.question: A ruling party permits voting but bans opposition candidates and independent reporting. Which evidence most undermines its democratic claim?
choices: It operates regional public schools
Voters lack meaningful political competition and information
It uses a written national constitution
It collects taxes to support public services
